blocks.html:
READING PASSAGE 3

You should spend about 20 minutes on Questions 27–40, which are based on Reading Passage 3 below.

The Robbers Cave Study

A review of a famous study into group behaviour

Group self-centredness seems to occur the minute people are divided into groups. It doesn't matter what the group is, or on what basis it was formed, we perceive the group we belong to as being superior to other groups and we develop an ‘in-group' bias.

Probably one of the most famous pieces of research looking at group behaviour was a field study conducted by Sherif in 1956. This study involved 22 boys aged between 11 and 12, who were divided into two groups. The groups were roughly matched in terms of sporting ability, camping experience and general popularity among their peers. Their parents were told that they were going to a three-week summer camp to see how well they would work alongside other boys when put into different teams. The parents were also told that the boys would not be allowed to be visited during that time, but would be able to go home if they wanted to. It was intended that the data for the study would be collected by participant observers.

At first, neither set of boys knew of the existence of the other set. They were taken to their respective campsites, which were located on a 200-acre, densely wooded area in Robbers Cave State Park, Oklahoma. The first week was spent doing a variety of activities, such as pitching tents and cooking. During this week, the two groups seemed to develop different group norms, one group being more 'tough' than the other, from which two boys went home early, as they were homesick. The groups were given a set of caps and T-shirts, and gave themselves names: the ‘Eagles' and the ‘Rattlers' (the latter being the tougher group).

At the end of the first week, they became aware of each other's existence by finding litter left by the other group or overhearing voices. Sherif noticed that already the groups had started to refer to the other group as 'them' and their group as 'us'. This marked the beginning of phase two of the experiment.

The groups were told that they were going to take part in a ‘Grand Tournament', which involved ten different sporting events, and they were shown the prizes for winning. The tournament was also to include in the final scores points which would be awarded for other activities, such as how tidy the cabins were kept. These scores were displayed on big scoreboards in what now became a joint hall where the two groups ate their meals together. This was necessary so the two groups would think they were on almost equal scores in the time leading up to the final event, which would increase the sense of competition. Needless to say, these scores were manipulated by the experimenters.

In order to check how high the levels of group self-centredness were in the groups at this time, a number of tasks were set up which involved the groups rating their own members and members of the other group. Each time, group members rated the boys in their own group much better at the tasks than the other boys, even though there was no real difference between them. They were also asked to rate all others in terms of how desirable they were as friends, and 93 per cent of friendship preferences were in-group preferences.

When the tournament started, the first game was basketball. The group that was thought to be less tough lost the game and claimed that they had lost only because the other group were bigger and older than they were. The Eagles won the next ball game and then were said to be cheating in the tug-of-war. This resulted in visits by both groups to each other's cabins over the course of the next 24 hours, where they ripped the mosquito nets, turned over the beds and generally made a mess. The Eagles devised a new weapon in the conflict which consisted of ‘rocks in socks' – and so it went on. Eventually, the Eagles won the tournament (with some help from the experimenters) and it was time for phase three to begin.

Research has suggested that the best way to reduce group conflict is by non-competitive contact. This required two conditions: that the groups had equal status and that they had a common goal to work towards. This was exactly what Sherif engineered. There were actually seven situations organised which gave the groups equal-status contact; these were things like having meals together or watching films together. The meals resulted in food fights; the films were enjoyed by both groups sitting totally apart from each other.

The other situations, where the groups had to work for common goals, had a much better outcome. These included raising money to go and see a film and solving problems, such as one with the water supply. The final common goal was a visit by truck to Cedar Lake to camp there before the end of the holiday. In this situation, although both groups travelled in separate trucks, another problem-solving situation arose when one of the trucks became stuck. All the boys joined in, using one of the tug-of-war ropes to help move it. At this point the group boundaries were beginning to disappear. On the final day, when they were due to return home, the boys themselves suggested that they travel in one bus and sat in friendship groups rather than as Eagles and Rattlers.

meta.title: The Robbers Cave Study (山洞)群体行为实验

passageNotes.label: Paragraph 1
passageNotes.text: 群体自我中心主义似乎在人们被划分为群体的那一刻就会发生。无论这个群体是什么，或者它是基于什么基础形成的，我们都认为自己所属的群体优于其他群体，并且我们会产生一种"内群体"偏见。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph 2
passageNotes.text: 研究群体行为的最著名研究之一可能是Sherif于1956年进行的一项实地研究。这项研究涉及22名年龄在11至12岁之间的男孩，他们被分为两组。这些群体在运动能力、露营经验以及在同伴中的总体受欢迎程度方面大致匹配。他们的父母被告知，孩子们将参加一个为期三周的夏令营，以观察他们在被分入不同队伍后与其他男孩合作的情况。父母们还被告知，在此期间不允许探望孩子，但如果孩子们愿意，可以回家。研究数据原计划由参与观察者收集。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph 3
passageNotes.text: 起初，两组男孩都不知道另一组的存在。他们被带到各自的营地位于俄克拉荷马州Robbers Cave州立公园内一片占地200英亩、树木茂密的区域。第一周用于进行各种活动，如搭帐篷和做饭。在这一周中，两组似乎发展出了不同的群体规范，其中一组比另一组更"强悍"，有两名男孩因为想家而提前回家。这些群体获得了一套帽子和T恤，并给自己取了名字："鹰队"和"响尾蛇队"（后者是更强悍的那组）。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph 4
passageNotes.text: 在第一周结束时，他们通过发现另一组留下的垃圾或无意中听到对方的声音而意识到彼此的存在。Sherif注意到，这些群体已经开始将另一组称为"他们"，将自己的群体称为"我们"。这标志着实验第二阶段的开始。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph 5
passageNotes.text: 这些群体被告知他们将参加一场"大奖赛"，其中包括十个不同的体育项目，并且他们看到了获胜奖品。比赛的最终分数还将包括因其他活动而获得的分数，例如小木屋的整洁程度。这些分数被展示在大记分牌上，记分牌放置在一个现在成为两组共同用餐大厅的地方。这样做是必要的，以便让两组在最终赛事临近时认为他们的分数几乎相等，从而增强竞争意识。不用说，这些分数是被实验者操纵的。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph 6
passageNotes.text: 为了检查此时群体中群体自我中心主义的程度有多高，设置了一些任务，要求群体对自己成员和另一组成员进行评分。每次，群体成员都给自己组的男孩在任务上的评分远高于另一组的男孩，尽管他们之间并没有真正的差异。他们还被要求从"作为朋友的吸引力"角度对所有其他人进行评分，结果93%的友谊偏好都是内群体偏好。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph 7
passageNotes.text: 比赛开始后，第一场比赛是篮球。被认为不那么强悍的那组输掉了比赛，并声称他们输球只是因为另一组的男孩比他们更高大、年龄更大。鹰队赢了下一场球赛，然后被指控在拔河比赛中作弊。这导致两组在接下来的24小时内互相闯入对方的小木屋，他们撕破蚊帐、掀翻床铺，基本上把一切都弄得一团糟。鹰队在冲突中设计了一种新武器，由"袜子里装石头"组成——就这样持续下去。最终，鹰队赢得了比赛（在实验者的某种帮助下），第三阶段即将开始。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph 8
passageNotes.text: 研究表明，减少群体冲突的最佳方式是通过非竞争性接触。这需要两个条件：群体地位平等，以及他们有一个共同的目标可以共同努力。这正是Sherif精心安排的。实际上，组织了七种让群体进行平等地位接触的情境；这些包括一起吃饭或一起看电影等活动。吃饭引发了食物大战；两组虽然都看了电影，但完全分开坐。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph 9
passageNotes.text: 其他需要群体为共同目标而努力的情境则取得了好得多的结果。这些包括筹钱去看电影和解决问题，例如供水问题。最后一个共同目标是在假期结束前乘卡车去Cedar Lake露营。在这种情况下，尽管两组分别乘坐不同的卡车，但当其中一辆卡车陷入困境时，又出现了一个需要解决问题的情境。所有男孩都参与进来，用一根拔河绳帮助移动卡车。此时，群体界限开始消失。在最后一天，当他们该回家时，男孩们自己建议乘坐一辆公交车，并按友谊分组而坐，而不是作为鹰队和响尾蛇队分开坐。

items.text:
（1）题目 27：（题干见题目区）
题目翻译：作者对参与该研究的男孩作出了以下哪两项陈述？
答案：A（They had approximately the same number of friends.）
定位：正文第2段，第3句
原文：The groups were roughly matched in terms of sporting ability, camping experience and general popularity among their peers.
译文：两组在运动能力、露营经验以及同伴中的总体受欢迎程度方面大致相当。

解析：roughly matched 对应 approximately the same，general popularity among their peers 对应男孩们的朋友/同伴情况，所以选 A。

（2）题目 28：（题干见题目区）
题目翻译：作者对参与该研究的男孩作出了以下哪两项陈述？
答案：E（They received clothes that identified the group they belonged to.）
定位：正文第3段，末句
原文：The groups were given a set of caps and T-shirts, and gave themselves names: the ‘Eagles’ and the ‘Rattlers’
译文：两组人都拿到了一套帽子和T恤，并给自己取名为“老鹰队”和“响尾蛇队”。

解析：caps and T-shirts 是收到的服装，结合 Eagles 和 Rattlers 两个组名可识别各自所属小组，所以选 E。

items.text:
（1）题目 29：The Grand Tournament marked the second part of Sherif’s experiment. It included a range of ________ that each team would compete in, and the allocation of extra points for things like cleaning cabins.
题目翻译：大锦标赛包括各队参加的一系列什么项目？
答案：sporting events
定位：正文第5段，第1句
原文：a ‘Grand Tournament’, which involved ten different sporting events
译文：一场“大锦标赛”，其中包括十个不同的体育项目。

解析：a range of 对应 ten different；各队 compete in 的对象是 sporting events。省略不改变中心指代的 sporting 后，events 也仍然语法、语义成立。段中的 activities 指清洁等额外计分项目，不是锦标赛中的比赛项目。

（2）题目 30：To increase the competitive element of the tournament, the organisers used ________ in the dining hall. They also made sure that the boys were under the impression that their scores were nearly ________ as the tournament neared its end.
题目翻译：组织者在餐厅使用什么来增强比赛的竞争感？
答案：scoreboards（big scoreboards）
定位：正文第5段，第3句
原文：These scores were displayed on big scoreboards in what now became a joint hall where the two groups ate their meals together.
译文：这些分数展示在大型记分牌上，记分牌位于两组一起用餐的公共大厅。

解析：used ... in the dining hall 对应 scores were displayed on big scoreboards in the joint hall，空格所指的展示物是 big scoreboards。

（3）题目 31：To increase the competitive element of the tournament, the organisers used ________ in the dining hall. They also made sure that the boys were under the impression that their scores were nearly ________ as the tournament neared its end.
题目翻译：锦标赛接近结束时，男孩们以为双方分数几乎怎样？
答案：equal scores（equal）
定位：正文第5段，第4句
原文：the two groups would think they were on almost equal scores
译文：两组都会以为双方分数几乎相同。

解析：题干已经用 nearly 改写 almost，因此空格只填 equal；若填 almost equal 会形成 nearly almost equal 的重复。

（4）题目 32：The ________, who were thought to be the tougher group, won the first ball game and lost the second. In other games there were accusations of ________. During the next day, various instances of conflict occurred within the boys’ cabins. Eventually, the tournament was won by the group that was considered to be ________ – the Eagles.
题目翻译：被认为更强硬、赢第一场球赛又输第二场的是哪一组？
答案：Rattlers
定位：正文第3段，末句
原文：the ‘Rattlers’ (the latter being the tougher group)
译文：“响尾蛇队”（后者是更强硬的一组）。

解析：Rattlers 是更强硬的一组；随后较弱组输掉第一场，Eagles 赢下一场，所以第一场赢家是 Rattlers。题干已有 The，只填专名 Rattlers。

（5）题目 33：The ________, who were thought to be the tougher group, won the first ball game and lost the second. In other games there were accusations of ________. During the next day, various instances of conflict occurred within the boys’ cabins. Eventually, the tournament was won by the group that was considered to be ________ – the Eagles.
题目翻译：其他比赛中出现了关于什么的指控？
答案：cheating
定位：正文第7段，第3句
原文：The Eagles won the next ball game and then were said to be cheating in the tug-of-war.
译文：老鹰队赢下下一场球赛，随后被指控在拔河比赛中作弊。

解析：were said to be cheating 改写为 accusations of cheating；介词 of 后填名词性形式 cheating。

（6）题目 34：The ________, who were thought to be the tougher group, won the first ball game and lost the second. In other games there were accusations of ________. During the next day, various instances of conflict occurred within the boys’ cabins. Eventually, the tournament was won by the group that was considered to be ________ – the Eagles.
题目翻译：最终赢得锦标赛的老鹰队原本被认为是什么样的一组？
答案：less tough
定位：正文第7段，第2句及末句
原文：The group that was thought to be less tough lost the game
译文：被认为较不强硬的那组输掉了这场比赛。

解析：这组随后被说明为 Eagles，而 Eagles 最终赢得锦标赛；空格需要完整比较级短语 less tough。只填 tough 会删除 less，并把“较不强硬”反转成“强硬”。

（1）题目 35：________
题目翻译：在地位平等、共同用餐的情形下，结果是什么？
答案：food fights
定位：正文第8段，末句
原文：The meals resulted in food fights
译文：共同用餐引发了食物大战。

解析：表格中的 eating 对应原文 meals，随之发生的冲突是 food fights。

（2）题目 36：________
题目翻译：在地位平等的接触中，哪一种活动让两组都喜欢、但仍分开坐？
答案：watching films
定位：正文第8段，末2句
原文：watching films together. The meals resulted in food fights; the films were enjoyed by both groups sitting totally apart from each other.
译文：一起看电影。共同用餐引发食物大战；两组都喜欢这些电影，但彼此完全分开坐。

解析：表格“Type of situation”要求活动类型，完整原文短语 watching films 同时与后面的 them 指代衔接。

（3）题目 37：A ________
题目翻译：能促成合作并形成友谊小组的另一个条件是什么？
答案：common goal
定位：正文第8段，第2句
原文：the groups had equal status and that they had a common goal to work towards
译文：两组地位平等，并且拥有一个需要共同努力实现的共同目标。

解析：表格与 Equal status 并列的另一条件是 A common goal；题干已给 A，所以填 common goal。

（4）题目 38：________, e.g. stuck truck
题目翻译：“卡车被困”是哪一类共同目标活动的例子？
答案：problem solving（solving problems）
定位：正文第9段，第2至4句
原文：solving problems, such as one with the water supply. The final common goal was a visit by truck to Cedar Lake to camp there before the end of the holiday. In this situation, although both groups travelled in separate trucks, another problem-solving situation arose when one of the trucks became stuck.
译文：解决问题，例如处理供水问题。最后一个共同目标是乘卡车前往 Cedar Lake 露营；途中一辆卡车被困，又出现了一个需要解决问题的情形。

解析：表格用 stuck truck 举例，原文把这类活动称为 solving problems，随后也出现 another problem-solving situation。三种连续原文形式均符合两词上限。

items.text:
（1）题目 39：（题干见题目区）
题目翻译：下列关于主持该研究的实验人员的陈述中，哪两项是正确的？
答案：C（They used a rating exercise to assess the amount of in-group bias.）
定位：正文第6段，第1句
原文：In order to check how high the levels of group self-centredness were in the groups at this time, a number of tasks were set up which involved the groups rating their own members and members of the other group.
译文：为了检查当时各组的群体自我中心程度，研究人员设置了若干任务，让各组评价本组成员和另一组成员。

解析：the groups rating their own members and members of the other group 对应 rating exercise，check how high the levels of group self-centredness were 对应 assess the amount of in-group bias，所以选 C。

（2）题目 40：（题干见题目区）
题目翻译：下列关于主持该研究的实验人员的陈述中，哪两项是正确的？
答案：E（They secretly altered some of the results of the tournament.）
定位：正文第5段，末句
原文：Needless to say, these scores were manipulated by the experimenters.
译文：不用说，这些分数被实验人员操纵了。

解析：the scores 指锦标赛期间展示并计入结果的分数，were manipulated by the experimenters 对应实验人员暗中 altered some of the results，所以选 E。
